newsitem.title: UK: UK housing boom gathers pace in July-Nationwide.
newsitem.headline: UK housing boom gathers pace in July-Nationwide.

text.p: Britain's housing market boom showed no signs of abating in July, with house prices rising 1.8 percent in the month, the Nationwide Building Society said on Thursday.
House prices are now 12.2 percent higher than in July last year and have reached the highest level since the end of 1989, when Britain was last in the throws of a housing boom.
Nationwide said house prices were being driven up by activity in south east of England.

"The apparent strength of house prices at the national level reflects continued strong gains in the south east, with signs that price pressures in London are shifting to the immediately surrounding area," said Paul Sanderson, Nationwide's head of research.
"The picture in other parts of the country remains far more subdued, and sales levels remain historically low everywhere, including London."
Nationwide expects sales to improve over the next few months as higher prices encourage more properties onto the market.
And recent rises in interest rates will not dent activity.
"Good affordability and improving confidence in the market suggests the recovery will weather the rise in mortgage rates seen over recent months," he said.
But the threat of further sharp rises in interest rates was a source of concern.
The Bank of England has raised interest rates three times in as many months to stand at 6.75 percent. The central bank meets next week to consider the level of rates again.
